Hello, I'd like to share a tool I've developed for exploring large formal proofs, and ask whether you think this approach could be useful or worth pursuing.

The idea is to represent Lean and Rocq developments as formal structural models, with a Datalog layer to explore dependencies, paths between theorems, and identify potentially important lemmas.

I've also experimented with small LLMs and graph analysis techniques to distinguish important from less important parts of a proof, and to generate short descriptions of mathematical statements.

The result is an interactive environment covering Fermat's Last Theorem, Navier–Stokes, the Prime Number Theorem, the four colour theorem, and others. You can double-click on lemmas, double-click on edges to explore their dependencies and navigate the proof.

https://arkitect-lab.k-inside.com/proofmaps/

This work builds on formal modeling research from my PhD and was developed independently of prove2me.

I'd really appreciate your feedback. Do you see value in this approach, and what would make it more useful for the theorem-proving community?
